# **Hypersensitivity reactions to contrast agents (in adults)**
An **immediate hypersensitivity reaction** occurs **within 1h** of contrast agent administration (rarely up to 6h), while a **non-immediate** hypersensitivity reaction occurs **between 1h and 1 week** (rarely up to 8 weeks) after administration.

# **Renal adverse reactions to gadolinium-based contrast agents**
MRI examinations The risk of CA-AKI is extremely low when gadolinium-based contrast agents are used in approved doses.
Radiographic examinations Gadolinium-based contrast agents are not approved for x-ray based angiographic examinations or CT.

# **Safe time intervals between contrast agent injections**
**When combining** contrast-enhanced CT or (coronary) angiography with an **iodine-** based contrast medium and contrast-enhanced MRI with a **gadolinium** -based contrast agent on the same day in elective situations, it is better to **start with** the **MRI** examination, unless the CT examination is intended for the kidneys, ureters, or bladder (CT Urography).
In patients with **normal renal function** (eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73 m²), consider a waiting time between elective contrast-enhanced MRI with GBCA administration and contrast-enhanced CT or (coronary) angiography with iodine-based contrast medium administration of optimally 6 h (near complete clearance of the effects of the previously administered GBCA) and minimally 2 h (if clinical indication requires rapid follow-up).
In patients with **moderate renal impairment** (eGFR 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m²), consider a waiting time between elective contrast-enhanced MRI with GBCA administration and contrast-enhanced CT or (coronary) angiography with iodine-based contrast medium administration of optimally 48 h (near complete clearance of the effects of the previously administered GBCA) and minimally 16 h (if clinical indication requires rapid follow-up).

# **Safe use of contrast agents in pregnancy and lactation**
**Pregnancy**
_Iodine-based contrast media_
In exceptional circumstances, when radiographic examination is essential, iodine- based contrast media may be given to the pregnant female.
Following administration of iodine-based contrast media to the mother during pregnancy, thyroid function should be checked in the neonate during the first week (neonatal testing of thyroid function is universal and routine in European countries).
_Gadolinium-based contrast agents_
When there is a very strong indication for enhanced MRI, the smallest possible dose of a macrocyclic gadolinium contrast agent may be given to the pregnant female.
Following administration of gadolinium-based agents to the mother during pregnancy, no neonatal tests are necessary.
**Lactation**
_Iodine-based contrast media_

...

_Gadolinium-based contrast agents_
Breast feeding may be continued normally when macrocyclic gadolinium-based contrast agents are given to the mother.
**Pregnant or lactating mother with renal impairment**
_Iodine-based contrast media_
See Prevention of contrast-associated acute kidney injury. No additional precautions are necessary for the fetus or neonate.
_Gadolinium-based contrast agents_
Do not administer gadolinium-based contrast agents.

...

# **Gadolinium retention in the brain and body**
**Gadolinium retention in the brain**
**Detection**
ׇ Seen as regions of increased signal intensity in the deep brain nuclei on unenhanced T1-weighed MR-images in patients administered GBCAs for prior MRI scans.

...

ׇ High signal intensity in the deep brain nuclei on MRI has been reported after all linear chelate gadolinium-based agents, but not after macrocyclic agents alone.

...

**Gadolinium retention in bone, liver and skin**
**Detection**
ׇ Requires biopsy and tissue analysis.
**Characteristics**
ׇ Occurs independent of renal function.
ׇ May occur after any agent but greater amounts are retained after non-ionic linear chelate gadolinium-based contrast agents.
ׇ Cannot be detected by MRI.
ׇ The amounts deposited are very small but greater than in the brain.

...

# **Safety of ultrasound contrast agents**
ׇ More severe acute reactions are rare and are like those after iodine- and gadolinium- based agents
**To reduce the risk**
ׇ Check for intolerance to any of the components of the contrast agent.

ׇ Approximately 10% more pregnancies and live births occur after HSG with oil-based contrast media compared to HSG with water-based contrast media
ׇ Image quality of HSG is significantly better when using oil-based contrast media

ׇ At present the amounts of gadolinium in surface and tap water are very low but they are likely to increase with increasing use of gadolinium-based contrast agents.
ׇ The risks of this gadolinium in the environment are not yet known.
